title: Mid-century
look: A 1950s modern cartoon: a loose ink line with one flat colour block printed out of register, on textured paper.

doc.essence: A modernist cartoon of the fifties: the drawing is a light, angular ink line, and the colour is a separate flat shape that does not quite land on it, over a couple of abstract background shapes.
doc.notIt: Not screenprint (the colour sits off the line, not under it; one colour, a line), not line-art (a colour block and paper), not rubber-hose (angular, thin line, limited animation instead of a bounce).
doc.shapes: The line traces every part's edge without filling it. Sharper corners, thinner tapering limbs, dot eyes and thin brows.
doc.colour: One flat colour, the body's, snapped to mustard, teal, coral, olive or sky, printed a few pixels off the line. The page shows through every other area.
doc.eyes: Small ink dots, a small mouth and thin brows.
doc.motion: Limited animation: poses hold, then move quickly to the next.
pitfalls: Overlapping parts show every edge, because nothing is filled: keep line weight light.
The colour block must stay offset by less than the line's gap to the next part, or it reads as a second character.
